description: Partie 3 — 16 conversations d'entraînement (dont 2 à trois locuteurs, 2 avec graphique, 4 questions de sens implicite).

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: Do you want to try the new Thai restaurant on Pine Street for lunch today?

transcript.speaker: Man
transcript.text: Sure. I heard it's very popular, though. We might have to wait for a table.

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: I'll call and reserve one for twelve fifteen.

transcript.speaker: Man
transcript.text: Great. I have a conference call until noon, so that works perfectly.

transcript.speaker: Man
transcript.text: Hi, I'd like to deposit this check into my savings account.

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: Certainly. Could you sign the back of the check for me first?

transcript.speaker: Man
transcript.text: Oh, sorry, I forgot. Here you go.

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: Thank you. The money will be available in your account tomorrow morning. Is there anything else I can help you with?

transcript.speaker: Man
transcript.text: Actually, yes. I'd like to order new checks. I'm moving next week, so they'll need to show my new address.

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: No problem. Just fill out this form with the new address, and the checks will be mailed to you within ten days.

transcript.speaker: Woman 1
transcript.text: OK, everyone, we need to finalize the holiday schedule. The store will open an hour early every day in December.

transcript.speaker: Man
transcript.text: I can take the early shifts. I'm a morning person anyway.

transcript.speaker: Woman 2
transcript.text: That would help me a lot. I take evening classes on Tuesdays and Thursdays, so I can't stay late on those days.

transcript.speaker: Woman 1
transcript.text: Noted. And remember, the busiest day will probably be the Saturday before the holiday. I need everyone here that day.

transcript.speaker: Man
transcript.text: Will we get extra breaks? Last year we were on our feet for ten hours.

transcript.speaker: Woman 1
transcript.text: Yes. Management has approved two extra fifteen-minute breaks for longer shifts.

transcript.speaker: Man
transcript.text: Sophie, do you know how to submit an expense report in the new system? I've been trying for twenty minutes.

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: There's a step-by-step guide on the intranet. I used it last week.

transcript.speaker: Man
transcript.text: I looked at it, but the screens don't match what I see.

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: Oh, they updated the system again on Monday.

transcript.speaker: Man
transcript.text: That explains it. I'll call the help desk, then.

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: Actually, Ken from finance is giving a short demonstration at three. You could join that.

transcript.speaker: Man
transcript.text: I'm looking for office space for my design studio. We're a team of eight, and we'd like to be close to the subway.

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: I have a space on Harbor Avenue that might interest you. It's two minutes from Central Station and gets lots of natural light.

transcript.speaker: Man
transcript.text: That sounds ideal. What's the monthly rent?

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: Four thousand dollars, including utilities. The building also has a shared rooftop terrace.

transcript.speaker: Man
transcript.text: That's a bit above our budget, but I'd like to see it. Are you free tomorrow morning?

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: I can show it to you at ten.

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: Hi, I'd like to order lunch for a team meeting on Wednesday. It's for fifteen people.

transcript.speaker: Man
transcript.text: Certainly. Have you had a chance to look at our platter menu?

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: Yes. Last time we had sandwiches, and people said they'd like something different. Several of our team members are vegetarian, too.

transcript.speaker: Man
transcript.text: Our pasta platter includes two vegetarian options, and it's very popular.

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: Perfect, we'll go with that. Could you deliver it by eleven forty-five?

transcript.speaker: Man
transcript.text: No problem at all.

transcript.speaker: Man
transcript.text: Excuse me, is this the train to Oxford?

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: It is, but it's been delayed by about twenty minutes because of a signal problem.

transcript.speaker: Man
transcript.text: Oh no. I have a job interview at eleven.

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: You should still make it. The journey only takes fifty minutes. You could also let them know you might be a few minutes late.

transcript.speaker: Man
transcript.text: Good idea. I'll send them an e-mail now.

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: Liam, I wanted to talk to you about the trade fair in Singapore next month. We need someone to run our booth.

transcript.speaker: Man
transcript.text: I'd be interested, but I've never been to Asia.

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: Well, you're the one who knows our new product line best.

transcript.speaker: Man
transcript.text: That's true. But I'd need someone to cover my accounts while I'm away.

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: Leave that to me. I'll ask Hana. She's handled your clients before.

transcript.speaker: Man
transcript.text: In that case, count me in. I'll start preparing the product demonstrations.

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: Hi, I bought these headphones here last week, and the left side has already stopped working.

transcript.speaker: Man
transcript.text: I'm sorry to hear that. Do you have your receipt?

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: Yes, here it is.

transcript.speaker: Man
transcript.text: Thanks. Since it's within thirty days, you can either exchange them for the same model or get a full refund.

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: I'd rather try a different brand. Do you have anything with better battery life?

transcript.speaker: Man
transcript.text: These over here last about forty hours on one charge. They're twenty dollars more, but you'd only pay the difference.

transcript.speaker: Man
transcript.text: Have we heard back from the city about the building permit for the library project?

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: Not yet. Apparently the planning office is short-staffed, so everything is taking longer than usual.

transcript.speaker: Man
transcript.text: That's a problem. The construction crew is scheduled to start on the first of next month.

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: I know. I've been thinking: we could ask the crew to start on the parking area first. That part doesn't require the permit.

transcript.speaker: Man
transcript.text: Good idea. That way we won't lose any time. Can you check with the site manager?

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: I'll call him right after lunch.

transcript.speaker: Man
transcript.text: Which session are you going to after the opening remarks?

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: I was planning to attend the digital marketing talk, but the speaker canceled this morning.

transcript.speaker: Man
transcript.text: Oh, that's too bad. Then why don't you come to the one I'm attending? It's about supply chains, and the speaker is excellent.

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: Sure, why not. Shall we meet outside the room ten minutes before it starts?

transcript.speaker: Man
transcript.text: Perfect. And I'll save you a seat if I get there first.

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: We just got a request from Brightline Consulting. They want to book thirty rooms for their annual retreat in October.

transcript.speaker: Man 1
transcript.text: Thirty? That's almost half the hotel. Which dates?

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: The ninth through the twelfth.

transcript.speaker: Man 2
transcript.text: There's a wedding party arriving on the eleventh. They've reserved twenty rooms.

transcript.speaker: Man 1
transcript.text: Then we'd only have twenty-five rooms available on those last two nights.

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: Maybe some of their staff could share rooms. I'll call their event coordinator and ask.

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: Did you see the e-mail from Ms. Alvarez? She wants the market analysis by Thursday instead of next week.

transcript.speaker: Man
transcript.text: Thursday? We haven't even received the survey data yet.

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: I know. The research firm said it would arrive on Wednesday at the earliest.

transcript.speaker: Man
transcript.text: Well, I'm not a miracle worker.

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: Should I ask her if we can send a preliminary version on Thursday and the full report later?

transcript.speaker: Man
transcript.text: Yes, please do. That seems like the only realistic option.

transcript.speaker: Man
transcript.text: Hi, I'm interested in joining the gym. What kinds of memberships do you offer?

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: We have monthly and annual plans. The annual plan works out about twenty percent cheaper.

transcript.speaker: Man
transcript.text: Do both include the swimming pool?

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: Yes, and group classes as well. If you sign up this week, you also get two free sessions with a personal trainer.

transcript.speaker: Man
transcript.text: That's tempting. Could I have a look around first?

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: Of course. Let me get someone to give you a tour.

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: Did you get the e-mail about the new phone system? It's being installed this weekend.

transcript.speaker: Man
transcript.text: I did. Will we get any training? The old system was so easy to use.

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: There's a twenty-minute online video, and the vendor is holding a question-and-answer session on Monday at nine.

transcript.speaker: Man
transcript.text: I have a client call at nine. Will the session be recorded?

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: I'm not sure. I'll ask Mr. Fujita. He's coordinating the installation.

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: Thanks for meeting with me, Mr. Davies. As I mentioned on the phone, our prices for packaging materials will increase by eight percent starting in January.

transcript.speaker: Man
transcript.text: Eight percent is a lot. We've been ordering from you for over ten years.

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: I understand, and we value your business. If you commit to a two-year contract, we could limit the increase to four percent.

transcript.speaker: Man
transcript.text: Hmm. A competitor offered us a similar deal last month, with free delivery.

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: Let me see what I can do about delivery. I'll talk to my manager and send you a revised proposal by Friday.

questions.prompt: What are the speakers discussing?
questions.explanation: La femme propose d'essayer le nouveau restaurant thaï pour le déjeuner.
questions.trap: La conférence téléphonique n'est qu'une contrainte d'horaire.

questions.prompt: What will the woman do?
questions.explanation: « I'll call and reserve one for twelve fifteen. »
questions.trap: « call » renvoie ici à l'appel au restaurant, pas à la conférence téléphonique.

questions.prompt: What does the man have until noon?
questions.explanation: « I have a conference call until noon ».
questions.trap: Le déjeuner a lieu après midi, à 12 h 15.

questions.prompt: Where does the conversation most likely take place?
questions.explanation: Dépôt de chèque, compte épargne, chéquier : ils sont dans une banque.
questions.trap: Le déménagement est mentionné, mais ce n'est pas le lieu de la scène.

questions.prompt: What does the woman ask the man to do first?
questions.explanation: « Could you sign the back of the check for me first? »
questions.trap: Le changement d'adresse intervient plus tard, pour les nouveaux chèques.

questions.prompt: Why does the man need new checks?
questions.explanation: « I'm moving next week, so they'll need to show my new address. »
questions.trap: « moving » se comprend ici comme « déménager ».

questions.prompt: What is the conversation mainly about?
questions.explanation: « we need to finalize the holiday schedule » : ils organisent les horaires de travail des fêtes.
questions.trap: « holiday » évoque une fête, mais il s'agit des horaires de la période des fêtes.

questions.prompt: Why can't the second woman work late on some days?
questions.explanation: « I take evening classes on Tuesdays and Thursdays ».
questions.trap: Les trois autres raisons sont plausibles mais jamais mentionnées.

questions.prompt: What has management approved?
questions.explanation: « Management has approved two extra fifteen-minute breaks for longer shifts. »

questions.prompt: What is the man trying to do?
questions.explanation: « do you know how to submit an expense report in the new system? »
questions.trap: L'intranet contient le guide, il ne doit pas le mettre à jour.

questions.prompt: What does the woman imply when she says, “they updated the system again on Monday”?
options: She was not told about the update.
The guide may be out of date.
The man should have attended a training.
questions.explanation: Les écrans ne correspondent plus au guide parce que le système a changé lundi : le guide est sans doute périmé. L'homme le comprend (« That explains it »).
questions.trap: Retenir seulement le fait technique sans le relier à la remarque précédente.

questions.prompt: What does the woman suggest?
questions.explanation: « Ken from finance is giving a short demonstration at three. You could join that. »

questions.prompt: Who most likely is the woman?
questions.explanation: Elle propose un local, en donne le loyer et organise une visite : c'est une agente immobilière.
questions.trap: Le studio de design est l'entreprise de l'homme.

questions.prompt: What does the man want to be close to?

questions.trap: Repérer la généralisation « subway » → « public transportation ».

questions.prompt: What does the man say about the rent?
options: It is higher than he planned.
It is cheaper than his current rent.
It must be paid in advance.
questions.explanation: « That's a bit above our budget » : le loyer dépasse ce qui était prévu.
questions.trap: Les charges sont incluses (« including utilities »).

questions.explanation: Elle choisit le plateau de pâtes (« we'll go with that »), à 14 $ par personne.

questions.prompt: What will the man most likely do next?
questions.explanation: « I'll send them an e-mail now. »
questions.trap: Il n'annule rien : il prévient seulement d'un éventuel retard.

To encourage the man to accept

questions.explanation: « I'd rather try a different brand. »

questions.prompt: What does the man say about the headphones he recommends?
questions.explanation: « They're twenty dollars more ».
questions.trap: « you'd only pay the difference » ne signifie pas qu'ils sont en promotion.

questions.prompt: What are the speakers discussing?
questions.explanation: Ils attendent toujours le permis de construire de la ville.
questions.trap: Le manque de personnel concerne le service d'urbanisme de la ville, pas leur entreprise.

questions.prompt: According to the woman, why is the planning office slow?
options: It does not have enough employees.
questions.explanation: « the planning office is short-staffed » = il manque de personnel.
questions.trap: Il faut connaître l'expression « short-staffed ».

questions.prompt: What does the woman suggest?
options: Beginning with a different part of the project
questions.explanation: Commencer par le parking, qui ne nécessite pas de permis.
questions.trap: Le report de tout le projet est justement ce qu'elle veut éviter.

questions.prompt: What problem does the woman mention?
questions.explanation: « the speaker canceled this morning ».
questions.trap: Le déjeuner figure au programme mais n'est pas évoqué.

questions.prompt: Look at the graphic. Where will the speakers meet?
questions.explanation: Ils iront à la séance sur les chaînes d'approvisionnement (« Supply Chain Trends »), en salle 5, et se retrouveront devant cette salle.
questions.trap: La salle 2 accueillait la séance de marketing digital, annulée.

questions.prompt: What does the man offer to do?
questions.explanation: « I'll save you a seat if I get there first. »
questions.trap: Il fait l'éloge de l'intervenant, mais ne propose pas de le présenter.

questions.prompt: Where do the speakers most likely work?
questions.explanation: Réservation de chambres, « almost half the hotel » : ils travaillent dans un hôtel.
questions.trap: Brightline Consulting est le client qui réserve.

questions.prompt: What problem do the speakers discuss?
questions.explanation: Avec le mariage, il ne reste que 25 chambres les deux dernières nuits, pour 30 demandées.
questions.trap: Le mariage n'est pas annulé : c'est lui qui occupe des chambres.

questions.prompt: What will the woman probably do next?
questions.explanation: « I'll call their event coordinator and ask. »
questions.trap: Changer les dates serait une solution possible, mais elle n'est pas proposée.

questions.prompt: What did Ms. Alvarez ask for?
questions.explanation: Elle veut l'analyse jeudi au lieu de la semaine prochaine : l'échéance est avancée.
questions.trap: Jeudi est la nouvelle échéance, pas une réunion.

questions.prompt: What does the man imply when he says, “I'm not a miracle worker”?
options: He disagrees with the survey results.
He has already finished the report.
questions.explanation: Sans les données, qui arriveront au mieux mercredi, finir pour jeudi est impossible : il juge l'échéance irréaliste.
questions.trap: Prendre l'expression au pied de la lettre.

questions.prompt: What will the woman probably do next?
questions.explanation: Elle propose de demander à Mme Alvarez d'accepter une version préliminaire jeudi ; l'homme approuve.
questions.trap: « preliminary version » est paraphrasé par « partial report ».

questions.prompt: Where are the speakers?
questions.explanation: « I'm interested in joining the gym » : ils sont dans une salle de sport.
questions.trap: La piscine fait partie des équipements de la salle.

questions.prompt: What is offered to people who sign up this week?
questions.explanation: « you also get two free sessions with a personal trainer ».
questions.trap: La réduction de 20 % concerne la formule annuelle, quelle que soit la semaine.

questions.prompt: What does the man want to do?
questions.explanation: « Could I have a look around first? » : il veut visiter avant de s'inscrire.
questions.trap: « That's tempting » n'est pas une inscription.

questions.prompt: What is the conversation about?
questions.explanation: « the new phone system … being installed this weekend ».
questions.trap: Le week-end est le moment de l'installation, pas le sujet.

questions.prompt: Why can't the man attend the session on Monday?
options: He has a call with a client.
questions.explanation: « I have a client call at nine. »
questions.trap: M. Fujita coordonne l'installation ; l'homme n'a pas rendez-vous avec lui.

questions.prompt: What will the woman ask Mr. Fujita about?
options: When the system will be installed
Whether a session will be recorded
questions.explanation: Elle ne sait pas si la séance sera enregistrée et va le lui demander.
questions.trap: La date d'installation et la durée de la vidéo sont déjà connues.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of the meeting?
questions.explanation: « our prices for packaging materials will increase by eight percent ».
questions.trap: Le contrat de deux ans n'est qu'une proposition en cours de négociation.

questions.prompt: Why does the man say, “We've been ordering from you for over ten years”?
options: To announce that he is changing suppliers
To ask for better terms as a loyal customer
questions.explanation: Il rappelle sa fidélité pour contester la hausse ; la vendeuse répond aussitôt par une offre plus avantageuse.
questions.trap: Lire la phrase comme une simple information chronologique.

questions.prompt: What does the woman say she will do?
questions.explanation: « I'll talk to my manager and send you a revised proposal by Friday. »
questions.trap: Elle ne promet pas d'annuler la hausse, seulement de revoir la livraison.
